NEXT: stage 3 - the cash-sleeve combine (capitulation book rides the trend books idle cash), shared-equity accounting, overlap drawdown measured; tests before it touches any live path. || Stage 3 PASSED (cash-sleeve combine, 30pct sleeve, capit enter 0.50, aligned equity curves): EVERY thin year lifts (2022 +3.1pp to 15.5, 2025 +2.6pp to 7.6, 2023 +2.9pp, 2019 +1.1pp; worst year 5.1 -> 7.6) AND combined drawdown FALLS in 6/8 years - 2021 dd nearly halves (17.4 -> 10.8): the bounce-buyer earns during the very crashes that draw the trend book down. Max combined dd 24.4 vs 26.1 trend-alone. CAVEAT: year-start sleeve overdraws cash up to 106.8pct in growth years (positions appreciate past the 0.50 entry ceiling); monthly rebalance fixes it and will shave those lifts slightly; thin years run 80-99pct use, feasible as-is. HONEST GAP: the combine is a stabilizer, not a rocket - 2019/2025 remain far below the 30pct floor; closing that gap still belongs to generation (P15/A60/A62) and to raising the capitulation books own expectancy (its sizing is naive equal-fraction). NEXT: engineer the combine properly (monthly rebalance, cash-capped sleeve, tests) and give the capit book the learned-sizing treatment. || Stage 3b (monthly rebalance + worst-bar cash cap, the FEASIBLE version) is BETTER than the naive sleeve: compounding the sleeve monthly turns 2021 into +113.8pp extra (dd 11.0 vs 17.4), thin years hold their lifts (2022 +3.3 to 15.6, 2025 +3.0 to 8.1, 2023 +3.2, 2019 +0.9), worst year 5.1 -> 8.1, max combined dd 24.3 vs 26.1, and the cash cap barely binds (avg r_m 88-100). Measurement phase COMPLETE. Remaining: live-path engineering (two-book orchestration + tests) and the capit books learned sizing - queued behind the P15 verdict and the operators adoption decision.

title: The new-information frontier opens: perp funding history + real Fear & Greed, feeding two modules built and waiting
rationale: Every price-derived generation lever is now a measured loss (P13 filters, P15 market features, P16/P17 labels, A61 committee) and the walk-forward mandate demands unseen-data performance. The two honest, free, point-in-time sources that feed ALREADY-BUILT modules: Binance USD-M funding settlements (crowd positioning; the microstructure module has waited for this feed since A06) and alternative.me Fear & Greed daily (real crowd emotion; the sentiment module currently uses a price proxy). Funding coverage starts ~2019-09 for BTC, later for alts - partial coverage is a fact to handle, not hide.
expect: Stage 1 (CPU map): funding extremes / F&G extremes stratify our champion trade outcomes or mark the bear-rally windows the sleeve buys. Stage 2: causal channels (bar reads only strictly-past settlements/days) + micro_gate / real-feargreed paired tests. Success signature under the NEW instrument: held-out walk-forward years improve.
kill: No stratification of realised outcomes at stage 1 (dies for the price of a download), or coverage too thin before 2020 to evaluate honestly.
impl: external_data.py (fetch+store verbatim, gitignored data dir). Consumers enforce causality: funding read strictly before bar time, F&G day strictly past.
result: Stage 1 PASSED on Fear & Greed; funding PARKED. Trend book by prev-day real F&G, 3,158 trades: Q1 fear -0.099pct/trade at 34pct win vs Q4 greed +0.956 at 48pct - near-monotone, a real losing tail our book does not avoid. DESIGN FINDING: the built sentiment module is CONTRARIAN (press on fear) and the real data says the OPPOSITE for a trend book - trend entries during fear days are counter-regime and lose; measuring before wiring saved us again. Capitulation book: best bounces at MID sentiment (+1.9/+2.2pct, 69pct win); panic-day entries ~breakeven (+0.05). Funding: U-shaped on trend, flat on sleeve - no clean signal, parked. STAGE 2: fng_min veto lever (prev-day real F&G below the indexs OWN published extreme-fear boundary of 25 - an external threshold, not fit to our map), new channel + module, off-by-default, tests; evaluated under the walk-forward instrument. || STAGE 2 WIN, and judged on the column that counts. Research years (P20, paired): fng_min 25 best arm +0.0045, both seeds positive, exposure DOWN 8.09->7.88. HELD-OUT years (P19's seven walk-forward nets, paired on identical nets): median -0.8% -> +2.0%, mean +17.3% -> +21.8%, negative years 4/7 -> 3/7. HONEST READING: the effect is concentrated - 2019 +2.8pp and 2021 +28.4pp - and is EXACTLY ZERO in 2022/2023/2024/2025, because in those years the book barely trades (exposure 1-4%) and rarely has an entry to refuse on a panic day. So this fixes a real leak in ACTIVE years and does nothing for the thin ones; it is a genuine improvement and not the answer to the 30% mandate. First lever built on non-price information, and the first to improve the held-out median.

title: Widen the universe to 24 DEEP-history symbols - A37's failure mechanism removed
rationale: Operator (2026-08-29): monitor more assets and only take the highest-certainty opportunities. A37 refuted a 35-symbol universe, but its mechanism was specific and is fixable: 'more coins means more chances for a spurious high-conviction signal on a noisy LATE-LISTED name to displace a good pick'. So the fix is not fewer symbols, it is deeper ones: this universe screens at 1,600 days of history (~4.4 years) and $5M turnover, giving 24 symbols that all actually EXIST across the held-out years. A37 also never tested the operator's real hypothesis - raising the certainty bar as the pool grows, so that a bigger pool buys selectivity rather than dilution.
expect: held-out years improve, most where the book is starved (2022/2025 traded ~52 times on unseen data); the mechanism to watch is mean conviction of EXECUTED entries rising
kill: wide loses again on the walk-forward column even with the raised bar - then breadth is genuinely not the constraint and A37's verdict generalises
impl: universe_deep.json (24 symbols) built; data downloading. Then a walk-forward campaign: train wide per cutoff, trade wide, sweeping enter in {0.75 (current), 0.80, 0.85} - judged ONLY on held-out years.
result: MEASURED on 6 of 7 cutoffs; the 7th (2025) was deliberately TRUNCATED on 2026-08-30 to free memory for the champion attempt the operator had prioritised - one more observation was not worth blocking his stated goal for hours, and that truncation is recorded rather than hidden. Held-out returns, wide(24) vs narrow(14): 2019 -42.5/-0.8, 2020 -25.2/-4.7, 2021 +153.6/+113.4, 2022 +1.2/-10.2, 2023 +2.0/-13.2, 2024 +37.0/+29.2 (at the shipping bar 0.75). VERDICT: breadth is CONDITIONAL on universe maturity. Where the added symbols had years of history (2021+), wide wins EVERY held-out year and has no negative year at 0.75 or 0.80, against narrow's two - the operator's all-years-green criterion, on unseen data. Where the list was young (2019/2020: only 8 and 15 trainable symbols) wide lost catastrophically, which is A37's mechanism confirmed rather than contradicted. 2026 sits in the mature regime, so the champion attempt runs on the wide universe.

title: Pyramiding: add to a position as it proves itself, never average down
rationale: Operator (2026-08-29): do not commit everything at once; scale in as more positive signals arrive. Verified gap - orchestrator entries were gated on `s not in positions`, so a held name could never be topped up regardless of how strong its signal became. The existing `money_pyramid` lever is ACCOUNT-level deployment, not per-position scaling; the name collided with the concept but not with the behaviour (the fifth name-vs-behaviour instance in this project).
result: BUILT: scale_in (tranches), scale_step (profit required since the last fill), scale_decay (geometric shrink). An add must clear the SAME bar as a fresh entry (conviction, veto, consensus) and the position must be IN PROFIT since its last fill - the single rule that separates pyramiding from averaging down. 7 tests including the explicit never-average-down case; suite 494. Off by default; measurement queued. || MEASURED AND REFUTED (P25, once the engine allowed the orders). Paired deltas: 1 tranche @0.55 -0.0157, 2 @0.55 -0.0243, 2 @0.45 -0.0230, drawdown 28.5% -> 34-36% in every arm. The per-year picture is the honest story: 2021 gains a spectacular +494pp, but 2019 loses 13.3pp (turning a POSITIVE year negative, -4.4%), 2020 loses 12.9pp, 2024 -5.5pp, 2025 -5.0pp, 2018 -4.5pp. It amplifies the moonshot and taxes everything else - the exact shape the judge was written to refuse. Mechanism: adding at +3% into a name whose conviction has already decayed buys the LATE part of a move, which is where the give-back lives; in a runaway year that is free money and in a normal year it is a worse average entry. The engine change stays (correct, opt-in, tested) and the lever stays off.
expect: more capital deployed into the trends that are working, without raising the number of distinct bets - the opposite of the refuted 'more exposure via worse trades'
kill: no lift on the held-out column, or drawdown rises faster than return

title: The untested mirror: keep the well-calibrated NARROW net, let it shop in a wider market
rationale: A66's first two cutoffs are brutal (2019 -42.5% vs -0.8% narrow; 2020 -25.2% vs -4.7%), and the mechanism is visible: a net TRAINED on 24 symbols produces conviction that is not comparable across them, so the top-2 pick is worse even though the pool is bigger. A40 already refuted train-wide/trade-narrow. The remaining cell is the operator's actual idea in its cleanest form: the net stays trained on the 14 it calibrates well, and only the SHOPPING LIST widens - inference is per-symbol, so a narrow-trained net can score names it never trained on. If its conviction transfers, breadth costs nothing and buys selectivity; if it does not, breadth is dead in all three directions and we stop paying for it.
expect: held-out years improve or at least hold, with more trades in the starved years
kill: transferred conviction is miscalibrated too (wide trades lose like A66) - then the breadth thesis is closed for good
impl: Reuse P19's seven walk-forward nets - NO training. Run infer.export over the 24 deep symbols per net, then evaluate each held-out year at enter 0.75/0.85. Cheap: inference only.

title: A symbol is not tradable until IT has history - the causal version of the universe screen
rationale: The wide candidate's only losing research year is 2018 (-6.8%), and the wide walk-forward's only disasters were 2019/2020 - precisely the years when most of the 24 screened symbols were freshly listed. The screen asks 'does this coin have 4.4 years of history?' ONCE, today; the book needs the answer AT EACH BAR. A coin with four years of history in 2026 had four months of it in 2018, and we were trading it as though the screen had vetted it. This is a real look-ahead of a subtle kind: not in the prices, but in the membership of the universe itself.
result: BUILT: modules/seasoning.py with lever min_age_days, vetoing any symbol whose own history at that bar is shorter than the threshold. Wired through orchestrator, strategy adapter and KNOWN_LEVERS; 6 tests including the exact 2018 failure shape. Off by default, so nothing changes until it is measured.
expect: the young-universe years stop bleeding - 2018 for the full-history candidate, and the 2019/2020 walk-forward cutoffs - without touching the years that already work
kill: the gate removes so many names that the book starves in the early years, trading the immature ones was not the cause, or the fix costs more in good years than it saves

title: On-chain network activity as a second non-price input
rationale: The fear veto is the only lever that ever improved the held-out column, and it came from information that is not price. This mines the same seam: four free, long-history daily series from blockchain.info describing NETWORK USE rather than price - unique addresses, transactions, hash rate, miner revenue - each read as a deviation from its own trailing trend, because a level is not a signal.
result: Stage 1 PASSED on two of four, on the champion's 3,329 round trips with strictly-past values only. Unique addresses: Q1 +0.107%/trade at 39% win rising monotonically to Q4 +0.867% at 47% - a spread of +0.76pp, comparable to the Fear & Greed spread that produced the adopted veto. Miner revenue: +0.006% to +0.720%, spread +0.57pp, though not monotone (Q3 above Q4). Transactions (+0.05pp) and hash rate (+0.18pp) carry nothing. CAVEAT recorded: blockchain.info downsamples long histories to roughly one point every four days, so this is a slow signal measured on a coarse grid - fine for a regime-style gate, useless for timing. || STAGE 2 REFUTED (P27, control healthy at +0.0563). Every arm negative and dose-ordered by strictness: -1.0sd -0.1208, -0.5sd -0.1091, -1.5sd -0.0445, with exposure falling 7.88% -> 6.55-7.77%. The gate does exactly what it was built to do - it refuses entries on quiet-chain days - and those refusals cost far more than they save. So the trade map was right that quiet-chain days have worse AVERAGE outcomes, and wrong as a basis for a veto: the trades it removes include the ones the year depends on. This is the same lesson P13 taught from the opposite direction (loosening the filter also loses), and it sharpens the rule: a per-trade average is not a licence to remove trades, because the distribution's right tail is where the years live.
expect: an 'activity gate' - refuse new entries when on-chain activity is unusually weak for its own recent history - lifting the held-out median the way the fear veto did
kill: the effect is a proxy for the fear index we already use (check the overlap before building), or it vanishes once the causal 4-day grid is respected in the channel

title: Sample the market on ACTIVITY, not on the clock - the one axis never touched
rationale: Everything this project has tested changes what the model SEES (features, labels, filters, sizing, universe, capacity). Nothing has changed WHEN it looks. Every bar is 15 minutes of wall clock, whether a million dollars traded or nothing did - so a dead night and a violent hour are the same observation, and the inputs are heteroscedastic by construction. Dollar/volume/CUSUM bars close a bar when a fixed amount of VALUE has changed hands, giving returns far closer to the i.i.d. assumption every estimator in this stack quietly makes. Two of our own measurements point here rather than away: A62 showed a coarser CLOCK holds strictly less material in every year (0.70-0.78x), which says the interval length is not the problem - the ruler is; and the thin years are thin at a FIXED cadence, while activity bars would spend fewer observations on the dead months.
expect: the net trains on a series whose statistics it actually assumes; the signature would be improvement concentrated in the thin years, where clock sampling wastes most of its observations on nothing happening
kill: aggregated dollar bars leave too few observations to train on at our history length, or the walk-forward held-out column does not improve - then sampling joins the list of things measured and closed
impl: Stage 1 (CPU, cheap): build dollar bars from the 15m data (aggregate until cumulative quote volume crosses a threshold chosen so the average bar count matches today's), then run the hindsight raw-rule map per year - the same gate that killed A62 in one afternoon. Only if the material is richer in the thin years does this reach the GPU.
result:
Stage 1 run, and the honest finding is about my own GATE rather than the idea. Dollar bars (threshold set so each symbol's bar count scales with its traded value) retain 93-95% of the harvestable long material in 2021-2025 while using only 41% of the observations - far better retention per observation than the 1h clock managed (70-78%). But NO year is proportionally richer: the thin years sit at 0.95, 0.93, 0.94, the same as the good ones. So the A62 half of the question is answered - activity sampling does not expose material the clock misses, because the material is a property of the price path and no ruler creates it.

What the gate CANNOT answer is what A72 actually claims. The proposal is not that dollar bars reveal more material; it is that they give the NET a series whose statistics match what every estimator in this stack assumes. A hindsight zigzag map measures price movement, not learnability, so passing or failing it says nothing about that claim. Recording this rather than dressing a mismatched test as a refutation - the P33 lesson, one level up: a gate that answers a different question than the one asked is not evidence.

Stage 2 is therefore a real GPU experiment (train on dollar-sampled bars, judge on the walk-forward held-out column), and it is worth the hours precisely because the retention number is encouraging: 94% of the material at 41% of the observations means a net trained on them sees nearly everything while spending far fewer parameters on dead time.

title: Per-indicator response curves: find each indicator's optimal value mathematically, then feed the tree a score or a binary barrier
rationale: Operator, 2026-09-02, with a worked example: if longs above the 200-period mean win 85% and below it 60%, sweeping the period 1..300 might reveal the true optimum at 162 - the maximum of a smooth response curve, found by calculus rather than by trying three values. Generalised: for every indicator in the A32 set, estimate the smoothed curve hit_rate(x) over the indicator's value using the attribution ledger's decision rows, locate its extrema, and expose the result to the decision tree as either an additional score or a binary barrier. The ledger built today is exactly the dataset this needs: every row already carries the indicator snapshot at the decision bar and the outcome. The mathematical names: univariate partial-dependence / marginal response estimation, with the optimum at the zero of the smoothed curve's derivative.
expect: Curves with a real interior optimum and enough support become levers; monotone curves justify simple thresholds; flat curves retire an indicator honestly.
kill: The trap is named in advance: sweeping many indicators over many values is a MULTIPLE-COMPARISONS engine, and the optimum of a noisy curve is selection bias in a lab coat (the P35 lesson: even four seeds disagree). So (1) curves are fitted on research years only, (2) an optimum must hold on walk-forward held-out years before it becomes a lever, (3) support floors like explain()'s min_leaf apply per bucket, and (4) anything adopted goes through the ordinary paired A/B with reseeds. If no curve survives walk-forward, the idea is measured and closed, not stretched.
impl: Stage 1 (CPU, cheap): extend attribution.py with response_curve(feature, rows) - kernel-smoothed hit rate over each A32 feature from the ledger's won/lost rows, bootstrap bands, report extrema with support. Stage 2: the surviving optima become a 'responsegate' module (score or veto) and one paired A/B decides adoption. Runs AFTER the width-192 champion attempt - one heavy job at a time.

title: Vector memory of past decisions: 'what happened the last N times the market looked like this?'
rationale: Operator, 2026-09-02: a vector database that helps the decision tree. The trade ledger already produces exactly its content - every decision bar with its 20-feature A32 snapshot AND its resolved outcome (won / lost / unforced / missed). Store those vectors and at each candidate entry retrieve the k nearest historical situations, then vote with their realised outcome. This is a genuinely different inductive bias from both the TCN (learned convolutions) and the tree (axis-aligned splits): non-parametric, local, and it can say 'no analogue found' - a form of honest abstention neither of the others has.
expect: Lift concentrated where the TCN is weakest: rare configurations it has few examples of. Also a natural confidence signal - the distance to the k-th neighbour.
kill: Leakage is the risk that kills this silently: a neighbour must be strictly in the PAST of the query bar and its outcome must have RESOLVED before the query bar, or the module is reading the future through a lookup table. Built with the same expanding time-purged walk-forward meta.py uses. If the walk-forward held-out column does not improve, it joins the measured-and-closed list.
impl: Stage 1 (CPU): build the store from attribution rows, standardise features, cosine/L2 index (sklearn NearestNeighbors - no new dependency), purge by resolution time. Stage 2: a `vectormem` module voting size_mult/veto from neighbour outcomes, one paired A/B. Runs after the participation work.
result: RETIRED by pre-registered kill criterion, 2026-09-05. Probe on 741,154 decision bars (14 champion symbols, tree's A32 features, tree's 8h forward label, 12 expanding blocks so neighbours are only ever already-resolved): memory k=25 edge +0.022 (51.3% top quartile vs 49.1% bottom, base 50.1%); a logistic regression under the IDENTICAL protocol - same admissible index rows, same standardisation, same outcome - edge +0.061 (53.6% vs 47.5%). The memory knows something, and a parametric fit on the same information knows it three times better: it is a worse tree, not a third inductive bias. Module + tests deleted per the kill criterion (recoverable from git history, commit d71bd96 and earlier); evidence in rnd/a74_vectormem_probe_2026-09-04.json. What would REOPEN it: a different memory - outcomes of the BOOK'S trades rather than raw bars, or distance used only as an abstention signal - is a new idea and files as one.

title: Attack PARTICIPATION, not the forecast: the ceiling says we take 0.03-5.9% of what our own constraints allow
rationale: tools/ceiling.py, 2026-09-02: with perfect foresight and every one of our own constraints and costs, 2026 pays +5,271% and 2022 pays +25,423%. We take 0.49% and 0.03%. Every gate in front of the entry - enter 0.75, breadth_gate 0.3, regime_deploy 0.5, fng_min 25, meta_margin, min_hold 16 - was last measured on the 64-CHANNEL net, and P35 proved that net was underfitting. A gate calibrated to protect a weak forecaster is exactly what should be re-opened once the forecaster gets stronger.
expect: If the 192-channel net is genuinely better, its convictions are better ordered, and the optimal entry bar moves DOWN. 2022 needs capture 0.03% -> 0.10% for a +30% year.
kill: P13 measured that loosening the filters loses - on the old net. If it still loses at 192 channels, participation is closed as a direction and the gap is genuinely the forecast, which sends the work to A73/A74 instead.
impl: P42, paired train_ab on the shipping genome: entry bar 0.75 vs 0.70 vs 0.65, then the gates one at a time. Judge on the walk-forward held-out column.
result:
HALF REFUTED, and the useful half survives. P42 tested the quality threshold: 0.70/0.65/0.60 all lose monotonically (-0.50 / -0.52 / -0.54) with drawdown going 19% -> 47%. So participation cannot be bought by accepting worse signals - P13's refutation holds at 192 channels under impact costs, and the entry bar is a genuine optimum.

What survives is narrower and better posed: the fit diagnosis says signals clearing 0.75 fire on 21% of bars at 77% precision, and the book holds two of them at a time. That is rationing by PORTFOLIO STRUCTURE, not by signal quality, and it is what A78/P44 tests. The distinction matters: 'trade worse things' is dead, 'trade more of the same good things at once' is untested.

title: Train on MORE markets, keep trading the same fourteen
rationale:
Operator, 2026-09-03: if the model needs more, train it on more data - other markets, even equities. The cheap half is already on disk: 27 symbols downloaded, 14 traded, so 13 unused series carry ~2.7M extra bars (+90% training data) at zero download cost.

The distinction that makes this NEW, because four experiments look like it and are not: A37/A40/A66/A68 all widened the TRADED universe and lost badly (median sealed 2026 -21%). None of them widened the TRAINING set while keeping the traded book narrow. Those are opposite claims - one says 'hold worse assets', this says 'learn from more examples of the same phenomenon and keep holding the good ones'. And it is exactly the textbook fix for the condition P35 proved we are in: underfitting.
expect: If capacity was binding and data is now the next constraint, the walk-forward held-out column improves and the thin years improve most, since they are where the model has seen fewest analogues.
kill: No improvement in the walk-forward held-out median -> the model is not data-starved and the constraint is elsewhere. A LOSS would also be informative: it would mean the extra symbols carry a different phenomenon rather than more of ours, which argues against the cross-asset stage before it costs anything.
impl: Stage 1 (P43, cheap, no download): train on all 27 local symbols, export signals and trade the same 14. One paired train_ab. Stage 2, only if stage 1 pays: pull more crypto symbols. Stage 3, only if stage 2 pays: cross-asset (equity index futures, FX) as PRE-TRAINING with a crypto fine-tune, since microstructure and session structure differ and mixing them raw is more likely to blur the target than sharpen it.
result:
REFUTED on both seeds. Training on all 27 local symbols while trading the same 14 gives a paired delta of -0.2858 (77101 +0.3437 -> -0.1010, 77102 +0.1559 -> +0.0289), with worst drawdown rising 19.6% -> 28.7% and exposure essentially unchanged (6.58% -> 6.95%). The variant provably engaged: the pooled panel went from 3,005,366 bars to 5,705,353, and the export still wrote signals for exactly the 14 traded names.

This fires the kill criterion written in advance, and it fires it usefully: the extra symbols carry a DIFFERENT phenomenon rather than more of ours. Pooling ICP, MOVR, DEXE, COTI and their peers pulls the shared representation toward assets we never trade, and the 14-name universe turns out to be not merely a good trading set but a good TRAINING set. Which kills the expensive stages before they cost anything: no more crypto downloads, and no cross-asset (equity / FX) pre-training, since the argument for those was exactly the one just refuted at the cheapest possible scale.

What is NOT refuted: 'more data helps'. What is refuted is 'more of THESE symbols helps'. The underfitting P35 found is still real - the remaining cure is capacity (P39), not breadth of source.

title: The operator's question: why is a backtest on the TRAINING data not almost perfect?
rationale: Operator, 2026-09-03: it does not seem normal that a backtest over the data we trained on is not nearly perfect. He is right that it is diagnostic. A model with enough capacity and enough passes SHOULD be able to memorise its training labels; ours reaches 66% validation accuracy and the ceiling measurement says we capture 0.03-5.9% of what perfect foresight would earn IN THE RESEARCH YEARS THEMSELVES. Three candidate explanations, and they call for different work: (1) the net still underfits - P34/P35 measured gains monotone in width and P37 died on hardware before finding the ceiling; (2) the labels are not learnable from 96 bars of causal price - the oracle uses hindsight the features cannot contain; (3) the gates in front of the net discard most of what it does get right, which is what P42 is testing.
expect: Measuring TRAIN accuracy against VAL accuracy separates (1) from (2) cleanly: a big gap means we memorise but do not generalise; a small gap at 66% means we cannot even fit the training labels, which is underfitting and points straight back at capacity and at A76's extra data.
kill: n/a - this is a measurement, not a proposal. It cannot lose, only inform.
impl: tools/fit_diagnosis.py: accuracy and oracle-capture on TRAIN windows vs VAL windows for the shipping net. GPU, minutes, runs when the queue frees.
result:
MEASURED. TRAIN accuracy 70.8% against VAL 66.2% - a generalisation gap of only 4.6%. The net does NOT memorise: after fifty passes it reaches 70.8% on data it has already seen. So the operator's intuition was right that an in-sample backtest ought to be far better than this, and the reason is the opposite of overfitting.

The number that reframes everything, though, is the precision AT THE TRADING BAR: conviction >= 0.75 fires on 21.1% of validation bars and is RIGHT 77.1% of the time (84.0% in-sample). The forecaster is not the weak link it looked like. With 14 symbols and ~35,000 bars a year, 21% of bars is on the order of 100,000 high-conviction bar-signals per year - and the book takes 90 trades. Whatever is losing the ceiling, it is downstream of the model.

title: Two slots cannot carry a signal that fires on a fifth of all bars - and sqrt-impact now REWARDS spreading
rationale:
fit_diagnosis (2026-09-03): conviction >= 0.75 fires on 21.1% of validation bars and is right 77.1% of the time. The book holds at most TWO positions at ~25% of equity each and averages 1.9-6.5% exposure, so it expresses almost none of what its own model is saying. The ceiling measurement agrees from the other side: 0.49% capture in 2026.

And the cost model just changed the arithmetic in this idea's favour. Impact is charged as 60*sqrt(participation), so splitting one order across four names costs sqrt(1/4) = HALF the impact per unit of capital that one concentrated order pays. Concentration was chosen when our own volume was free; it is a different trade now that it is not.
expect: More slots at smaller size raises exposure and total impact cost sublinearly while raising the number of 77%-precision signals acted on. The thin years should gain most - they are where the book sat in cash while signals existed.
kill: If more slots lowers the score, the signal's precision does not survive being acted on more often - which would mean the 77% is concentrated in the very top convictions and the book is already taking exactly those. That is a real and useful answer: it would send the work to the forecaster (A76 data, P39 capacity) and close portfolio structure.
impl: P44, paired risk arms on the same trained nets: max_positions 2 vs 3 vs 4 vs 6, and a deployment arm, judged on the score and the thin years with drawdown reported.
result:
REFUTED, but the clean arms are confounded and the honest answer comes from one arm only. Raw deltas: 3 slots -0.0896, 4 slots -0.1237, 6 slots -0.1622, both seeds worse every time.

MY DESIGN ERROR, stated rather than buried: position size is equity * deploy / max_positions, so adding slots SHRINKS every position. Exposure fell 6.55% -> 6.06% -> 5.42% -> 4.32% as slots rose. Those arms therefore tested 'smaller positions', not 'more names at the same commitment', and their monotone loss is largely a book that deployed less capital.

The one arm that controls for it is '4 slots + deploy 0.70', which restores exposure to 6.92% against the baseline's 6.55% - close enough to read. It loses -0.0710 with both seeds down (+0.3533 -> +0.2437, +0.1567 -> +0.1242). That is seven times the ~0.01 noise floor, so at MATCHED exposure spreading across more names still loses. The answer stands; only the size of the effect was inflated by the confound.

Reported trade-off, since the operator asked for drawdown to be minimised without gutting returns: more slots buys a genuinely calmer book. Worst drawdown falls 19.15% -> 16.84% -> 13.76% -> 12.16%, and '4 slots + deploy 0.70' gives 16.83% for -0.071 of score. Not adopted - it is a real option to hold, and the operator's call, not mine.

CONSEQUENCE: the kill criterion written in advance fires. The book is NOT rationing good signals - the edge really does live in the very top convictions it already takes, and both halves of the participation thesis are now closed (P42 quality, P44 breadth of holdings). Everything downstream of the model has been measured and is right where it should be. The work returns to the forecaster, alone.

title: Retry the wide training set with ONLY the liquidity-matched extras (LTC, BCH, AVAX, UNI, AAVE, XLM) - and treat it as the fishing expedition it is
rationale: P43 pooled all 13 spare symbols at once, and several of them (MOVR, DEXE, ONG, COTI) are thin, late-listed coins whose behaviour our 14 names do not share. A liquidity-matched subset is a different and more defensible hypothesis: add examples of the SAME phenomenon rather than more phenomena.
expect: if dilution was the mechanism, a matched subset should be neutral-to-positive
kill: Explicit multiple-comparisons warning, written before running: P43 already tested 'more symbols' and lost, so re-cutting the same 13 symbols until a subset wins is exactly how a project fools itself. This runs ONCE, on a subset fixed by a liquidity rule stated in advance (median bar value within 3x of the traded universe's), on the standard two seeds. No second cut. If it loses, breadth of source is closed permanently.
impl: one paired train_ab, subset chosen by rnd/impact_calibration.json's median bar values - a rule, not a search.

title: 2025 is the only losing year and the operator does not believe it - find the mechanism, then build the rail that detects it EARLY
rationale:
Operator, 2026-09-03: "veo que 2025 tiene perdidas, que no es nada normal... no me creo que de golpe aparezca un ano en el que tengamos perdidas, asi que hay algo que cuesta mal. O hay que intentar prevenir que puede pasarle a un ano asi... para detectar donde nos estamos equivocando y prevenir esos trades."

The forensics say it is NOT a fluke of the market and NOT a broken year of data. 2025 offered +21,958% across 3,571 opportunities - more raw material than 2023 (+12,177%, 2,114 legs) which we turned into +73%. The failure is ours, and it has a precise signature:

  year   ret      trades  per-trade   oracle per-trade
  2022  +8.68%       47    +0.177%        +0.625%
  2023 +73.01%      158    +0.348%        +0.702%
  2024 +155.72%     324    +0.290%        +0.527%
  2025  -2.96%       75    -0.040%        +0.533%

2025 is the ONLY year whose average trade is negative. It is not that we traded too little (2022 traded less and still made money) or that the edge vanished from the market (the oracle's per-trade is normal, +0.533%). We entered 75 times and were wrong on average every time - the selector kept firing while its precision had gone.
expect: Two separable causes, and the ledger can tell them apart: (a) REGIME - 2025's up-swings are shorter or choppier than the trend filter assumes, so entries are systematically late and stops take them out; (b) DECAY - the net's conviction is miscalibrated on 2025 specifically (it is the last research year, furthest from the bulk of the training mass). Distinguish by comparing conviction-vs-outcome calibration in 2025 against 2018-2024 using tools/fit_diagnosis.py per year.
kill: If 2025's per-trade loss is NOT explained by either regime or calibration - if the entries look identical in every measurable respect to 2023's and simply lost - then there is no rail to build and the honest conclusion is that one year in nine goes against a long-only trend book. Say so plainly rather than inventing a filter that only fits 2025; a rail fitted to the one bad year in the sample is the purest form of overfitting this project can commit, and it would be invisible until it cost real money.
impl: Stage 1 (diagnosis, no adoption): per-year fit_diagnosis + the trade ledger (attribution.py) restricted to 2025 - what did the losing entries have in common, and did any published indicator separate them BEFORE entry? Stage 2 (the rail): only if stage 1 finds a signal that is present in 2025 AND harmless in the other eight years - the rail must be judged on all nine, never on the one it was built for. A79/A39 (live edge monitor) is the natural shape: cut exposure when realised per-trade edge decays, which is regime-agnostic and would have fired in 2025.

title: Split breadth_gate in two: stop BUYING in a bear without being forced to SELL
rationale:
breadth_gate currently does two things with one number: it vetoes new entries AND demands every open position to cash. Those are not the same decision. Refusing to buy into a collapsing market is cheap - you simply do not act. Being forced to sell is expensive twice over: it realises the position at whatever the bottom of the breadth dip happens to be, and it pays the round-trip cost to get back in when breadth recovers.

That second cost is the shape of 2025. The year has the best hit rate in the ledger and still finishes negative, which is exactly what repeated forced exits and re-entries look like: the entries were right, the holding was interrupted. gate_forensics shows the switch was on for 52.9% of the year's signals.

So: keep the entry veto, make the flatten-the-book demand a separate lever. In a broad crash - 2018, 2022 - both should fire. In a choppy year where breadth dips under the line and recovers, only the first should.
expect: 2025 and 2023 improve (choppy years where breadth crosses the line repeatedly); 2018 and 2022 are roughly unchanged if the entry veto alone is what saved them, and WORSE if the forced exit was doing the real work there. That second outcome is the informative one and would say the two jobs genuinely belong together.
kill: Killed if the worst calendar year does not improve, or if 2018/2022 give back more than 2023/2025 gain on the consistency score. Also killed cheaply and early if P48 shows that simply lowering breadth_gate already captures the whole effect - then this is extra machinery for an effect a number already bought.
cost: one new risk lever + a paired run; no retraining

title: consensus_k has been 1 for the entire history: the consensus filter has never refused a single entry
rationale: gate_forensics counts no_consensus = 0 in every one of the eight research years. The lever exists, the modular ensemble was built partly to support it, and it has never once been binding. That is not evidence it does not work - it is evidence it has never been tried.
expect: consensus_k = 2 cuts the eligible count hard in every year. Given P46 just measured that removing the marginal trades removes profit, the honest prior is that this LOSES - but it removes them by a different criterion (agreement between modules rather than the height of one score), and that is a genuinely different question from the one P46 answered.
kill: Killed if it loses on the consistency score, like the entry-bar family did.

title: Search the thresholds JOINTLY with Bayesian optimisation (TPE), instead of one lever at a time
rationale:
OPERATOR'S IDEA, 2026-09-04, and it names a real gap: 'all these modules have fixed values - conviction at 0.75 and so on. There will be combinations of thresholds that do better than the current ones. Could we not run a mathematical simulation that adjusts and varies these values - not testing all the millions of combinations, but approximating, so instead of moving one threshold digit by digit a function gets close to the winning formulas without trying them all.'

That is Bayesian optimisation; the algorithm is TPE (Bergstra 2011) via Optuna.

What already existed, so the gap is stated honestly: the NN genome IS searched by a genetic algorithm (autoloop._evolve), and the band IS swept 72 ways inside train(). The risk layer, however, is a HAND-WRITTEN LIST OF NINE TUPLES over four dimensions (RISK_GRID: max_positions, position_fraction, stop_loss, trail_stop). Of the twelve thresholds the champion actually runs on, four have ever been searched - along nine points of a coarse axis-aligned grid - and EIGHT have never been searched at all. breadth_gate, regime_deploy, meta_margin, fng_min and money_model were each set by a separate one-lever experiment and frozen. Nothing in this project's history has ever looked for an INTERACTION between two of them. The operator's instinct is right and the gap is bigger than he supposed.
expect:
Honest prior, written before the first result: the FIT score improves a lot and most of it does not transfer. Eleven continuous dimensions against six years is the most efficient overfitting machine this project has built, and it has been fooled four times by far weaker selection. What makes the run worth doing is that the design can MEASURE that: years 2018-2023 are fitted, 2024-2025 are held out and recorded on every trial without ever entering the objective. If the held-out gain is flat, the answer is that the thresholds are already at a point that generalises - which is itself worth knowing and has never been established.

The rank correlation between fit and held-out score across all trials is the diagnostic: near zero means the surface is noise and no amount of further search will help.
kill:
Killed if the held-out score does not improve over the champion's. NOT killed for a disappointing headline: a study that proves the current point already generalises closes a large question and stops a whole family of future ideas.

2025 is deliberately in the HELD-OUT half even though it is the year we want to repair - optimising on it is how we would fool ourselves about having repaired it. 2022, the other quiet year, is in the fit half, so a threshold set that understands quiet markets is still findable and will have to prove it on a year it never saw.
impl: PYTHONPATH=trading-system python research/system06/tools/numerical_optimization.py --trials 300
cost: ~4.6 min per trial x 300, three CPU workers, no GPU - runs beside training
result:
THE BEST RESULT OF THE DAY AND STILL NOT A CHAMPION, on a stricter reading than the raw returns suggest.

  RESEARCH (192x3 shipping net, optimised thresholds, study trial 51)
  2018 +318.38%  2019 +180.98%  2020 +262.84%  2021 +40750.61%
  2022  +23.01%  2023  +75.47%  2024 +151.74%  2025     +4.09%
  score +0.3619 (incumbent +0.1763)  worst year +4.09% (incumbent -2.96%)
  ALL YEARS POSITIVE - the incumbent is not

  SEALED 2026   +20.39%  maxDD 12.86%  145 trades  exposure 1.32%
  incumbent     +25.71%  maxDD 22.13%   90 trades

Lower return on the sealed year, by 5.32 points. Also barely more than HALF the drawdown, 12.86% against 22.13%. Return per point of drawdown: 1.59 against 1.16.

The operator's balance criterion is stated for the opposite case - a gain merely proportional to its extra drawdown is not worth taking - and applied in mirror it reads clearly: the incumbent's extra 26% of return costs 72% more drawdown. That is a disproportionately expensive advantage. But the criterion is the operator's to apply, not mine, and the stated success test is the forward RETURN, which this does not beat. Recorded as not adopted.

WHAT SURVIVED SCRUTINY, because the headline is the least interesting part:

  - It transfers in time. Fitted on 2018-2023 with 2024-2025 never shown to the sampler; holdout score +0.1028 against the incumbent's +0.0280.
  - It is not a lucky point. 57 of 87 trials beat the incumbent on the held-out half; the top-20 region median holdout is +0.115 at a median drawdown of 18.8%, BELOW the incumbent's 20.8%.
  - It is not leverage. Average exposure 6.75% -> 7.25%, and per year it goes DOWN in six of eight while returns rise in all of them. Same stake per name (0.1667/3 = 0.0556 against 0.15/2 = 0.075), spread wider.
  - It transfers across NETS. Run against three nets it was never tuned on it wins 3/3, including prev_champion_64ch, a different architecture: +0.2451 there, +0.0531 on _candidate, +0.0397 on the fresh 256x3. So it is not co-adapted to one export's calibration - the failure the held-out years could not have caught.

AND IT SETTLES THE METHOD QUESTION THE OPERATOR RAISED. Eight of the twelve live thresholds had never been searched at all, and no interaction between any two had ever been tested. The joint optimum picks max_positions 3 with position_fraction raised to hold the per-name stake - which is precisely the combination P44 could not test, and whose absence P44's own writeup recorded as a confound. Every single-lever refutation in this ledger that touches a denominator of sizing is now unproven rather than closed.

title: Nothing enforces a single GPU job; two trainings on the 8GB card thrash instead of failing
rationale:
Measured 2026-09-04: with the champion-256 build and the experiment runner both training, the card sat at 7786/8188 MiB and 49% utilisation - thrashing. Killing one took it to 6577 MiB and 100%. The failure mode is the worst kind, because it does not error: both jobs keep running, roughly ten times slower, and every heartbeat looks healthy.

The STOP_AUTOTEST brake exists but is manual in both directions. Setting it is a person noticing; clearing it is a person remembering. An unreleased brake is indistinguishable from a dead lab. The pulse now reports a held brake every hour, which makes the landmine visible - it does not remove it.
expect: A file lock taken by whoever trains and released on exit, with the runner waiting on it rather than a person setting a stop file. The heartbeat then says 'waiting for the GPU' instead of going quiet, which is a true statement rather than an absence.
kill: Not a hypothesis; it either exists or it does not.

title: The two improvements are orthogonal: optimised thresholds ON the 256-channel net
rationale:
P47 changed the net and kept the thresholds. A83 changed the thresholds and kept the net. The cross-net check already scored the combination on RESEARCH years - it was one of the three nets tested - and it is the highest research score anything has reached here: +0.5598 with all years positive at a 14.8% worst drawdown, against +0.5201 for the 256 net alone and +0.3619 for the thresholds alone.

That number was computed in crossnet_check.py, which was authored and launched BEFORE either sealed readout existed, so the combination is not a candidate chosen because the other two disappointed on 2026.
expect: Honestly uncertain, and the day gives reasons both ways. Both components improved the research half and both LOST on the sealed year, which is a warning that this research surface and the forward year have come apart. The combination could inherit both forward losses as easily as both research gains. Its worst research year is +9.85%, below the 256 net's own +25.22%, so it is not uniformly better even on the half it was measured on.
kill: One sealed readout, taken deliberately and not today. Three windows were opened on 2026 in a single afternoon, and choosing what to read next BECAUSE the last two disappointed is how a seal decays into a selection input by increments that each look reasonable. Adopted only if the forward return beats +25.71%.
cost: one backtest, no training - the net and the thresholds both exist

title: Both of today's candidates doubled the research score and LOST on the sealed year. The selection instrument may be measuring the wrong thing
rationale:
P47: research +0.1763 -> +0.5201, sealed 2026 +25.71% -> +10.25%.
A83: research +0.1763 -> +0.3619, sealed 2026 +25.71% -> +20.39%.

Two independent routes - a wider net, and a joint threshold search - both large wins on 2018-2025 and both losses on 2026. That is not two unlucky draws, it is a pattern, and it points at the OBJECTIVE rather than at either candidate.

The consistency law is worst_year + 0.10*CAGR, and CAGR over a record containing 2021 at +40750% is dominated by a single moonshot year. A search maximising it will prefer configurations that hold on through explosive trends, and 2026 has not been such a year. A83's own numbers show the shape: 2021 goes from +14554% to +40751% while 2025 gains four points.
expect: A score that weights years equally - median annual return, or the worst year alone, or log-return CAGR with 2021 winsorised - should rank candidates differently. The test is cheap and needs no new backtests: rescore the 96 completed A83 trials under each alternative objective and check which one's ranking correlates best with the HELD-OUT half. That is a direct measurement of which objective generalises, on data already sitting in the study database.
kill: Killed if no alternative objective ranks the held-out half better than the current one. Then the objective is fine and the gap is elsewhere.
cost: no compute - rescoring rows already in optuna_thresholds.db

title: A macro state channel: inflation, rates, growth, oil - as a SIZE and VETO input, never as a direction call
rationale:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-04, verbatim in substance: 'what I also want is an INTELLIGENT system - one able to read and understand the market, to increase positions when we are on a run and reduce them when there is risk, to hold as much information as possible at once. Inflation data is probably directly related to market direction: real-time Fed news, US Treasury, GDP readings, all the economic data, the oil price, geopolitical wars, the news. All of that can anticipate trends. I know we trade short-term, intraday or swing, but sometimes there are things that affect us: if there is a risk two or three days out that the market collapses because of geopolitical tension, maybe at those moments the trades should be smaller, or there are moments when trading should stop altogether.'

The half of this that is cheap and testable first: SCHEDULED macro data. CPI, FOMC decisions and minutes, non-farm payrolls, GDP releases, and the oil price are published on a known calendar with known values, they are free from FRED and the BLS, and they are not text - so this needs no language model and no news scraping to get started. That matters because the expensive, ambiguous half (news, geopolitics) can then be judged against a baseline that already exists rather than being the whole bet.

It enters as a MODULE in the existing ensemble - one more voter alongside regime, fractal and crowd - so it can size, veto or scale deployment and can never invent a direction of its own. That is the architecture's own rule and it is the right one here: a macro reading that says 'risk is high' is a statement about VARIANCE, and turning it into a price forecast is exactly the overreach that makes macro overlays fail.

It also has to survive the seal. Macro series get REVISED - the GDP print you see today is not what was published that morning - so a backtest that reads the current value of a 2019 release is reading the future. Every series must be taken point-in-time (FRED's ALFRED vintages) or the whole result is a lookahead artefact dressed as insight.
expect:
Concretely falsifiable: exposure should fall in the days around CPI and FOMC prints and in months when real rates rise, and the effect should show up as a HIGHER worst year and a higher share of winning months, not as a higher CAGR. If it only lifts the average it is a leverage knob with a macro label on it.

Honest prior: crypto's relationship to macro is regime-dependent and was close to nil before roughly 2020. Six of our eight research years may carry no signal at all, which would make this a 2023-onwards lever tested on very little data - a reason to hold it to the held-out half rather than to the fit.
kill:
Killed if the held-out half does not improve, or if the effect is only present in the fit years. Killed immediately if the only gain is a higher CAGR at an unchanged or worse worst year - that is the failure this project made twice on 2026-09-04.

NOT built at all until point-in-time vintages are wired, because a version that reads revised data cannot be distinguished from one that works.
cost: medium - FRED/ALFRED loader, one module, one paired run; no GPU

title: Real-time news and geopolitical tension as a risk-off input
rationale:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-04, verbatim in substance: 'what I also want is an INTELLIGENT system - one able to read and understand the market, to increase positions when we are on a run and reduce them when there is risk, to hold as much information as possible at once. Inflation data is probably directly related to market direction: real-time Fed news, US Treasury, GDP readings, all the economic data, the oil price, geopolitical wars, the news. All of that can anticipate trends. I know we trade short-term, intraday or swing, but sometimes there are things that affect us: if there is a risk two or three days out that the market collapses because of geopolitical tension, maybe at those moments the trades should be smaller, or there are moments when trading should stop altogether.'

The expensive half of A87, deliberately separated so it cannot hide inside it. Text needs a source, a licence, a point-in-time archive and a model to read it, and each of those is a place for the future to leak in - a headline archive assembled today is not what was readable that morning, and a sentiment model trained on recent text has read the outcome of every event in our research years.

Sequenced AFTER A87 for a reason that is about evidence, not effort: if scheduled macro data - clean, free, unambiguous, point-in-time - carries no signal for this book, then unstructured news almost certainly does not either, and we would have learned it for a fraction of the cost.
expect: A tension index that raises cash ahead of drawdowns. The measurable claim is narrow: on the twenty worst weeks of the research record, does the index rise BEFORE them more often than chance? That is checkable before a single line of trading code.
kill: Killed if the index cannot beat chance at anticipating the worst weeks - a pure measurement, no strategy involved. Killed if no point-in-time text archive can be obtained, because the alternative is a backtest that reads the future.
cost: high - archive, licence, model, and a lookahead audit

title: Press when the book is winning, shrink when it is not - measured against the levers that already do this
rationale:
The operator's phrase, 2026-09-04: 'able to increase positions when we are on a run and reduce them when there is risk'.

Stated honestly, this is already SEVERAL levers in the brain, and every one of them is currently OFF: money_pyramid (anti-martingale deploy scaling from the equity trend), dd_sizer (taper as the drawdown limit nears), edge_monitor (cut deploy when our own realised edge decays), scale_in (pyramid into a winning position), vol_scale (target volatility). Each was switched off by an experiment that tested it ALONE against a book tuned for its absence.

A83 is the reason to reopen them rather than build a sixth: every one of these is a multiplier on a deployment fraction that other levers also move, so testing one in isolation measures almost nothing - which is exactly how P44 refuted 'more slots' and was then contradicted by the joint search. The 33-lever study now varies all five together for the first time in this project's history.

So this item is NOT 'build adaptive sizing'. It is: read what the joint search does with the five adaptive-sizing levers it already has, and only build something new if the search turns them all off.
expect: One of two answers, and both are worth having. Either the search switches some of these ON - in which case the operator's instinct is confirmed by measurement and the capability was already in the code, unused - or it leaves them all at zero, which is the first real evidence that this family does not pay on this book and makes the case for a NEW mechanism rather than a sixth variant of an old one.
kill: Not a hypothesis to kill; a reading to take. It closes when the study has enough trials to say which of the five the search keeps.
cost: none - already inside the running study

title: Research-year performance is nearly worthless as evidence; every promotion must be argued on OUT-OF-SAMPLE data
rationale:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-04: 'a system that gets great results on the data it was trained on does not surprise me - that is what we should be doing. The only place the quality and capability of this system is measured is 2026, where we have not trained the model, where everything is new to it and it is improvising as it goes. Ten percent does not strike me as remarkable at all... the fact that it makes 14,000% or 80% in the past worries me little.'

The day's evidence is entirely on his side. Two independent routes - a wider net and a joint threshold search - each roughly doubled the research score, and each LOST the sealed year: +10.25% and +20.39% against the incumbent's +25.71%. A metric that moves that much while the only honest measurement moves the wrong way is not measuring skill.

The consequence is procedural and it changes what a 'result' means here. A candidate's research numbers are context, not evidence. The evidence is: does the improvement hold on years the tuning never saw? So the search fits 2018-2023 and 2024-2025 are recorded on every trial and used for nothing until one final confirmation - they stand in for 2026 precisely because they are what 2026 will be, the years after the ones we tuned on.

And the target is stated in the operator's own order of priority: never lose a year, win as many MONTHS as possible, and at least +30% in 2026.
expect: The held-out score becomes the headline everywhere it is reported, and any candidate whose fit improves while its held-out score does not is refused - including candidates that look spectacular on the research record.
kill: Not falsifiable; it is the method. Revised only by the operator.
cost: none - it is a rule about what counts

title: adaptive sizing levers, varied jointly
result: ANSWERED, negative. All five of the operator's 'size up on a run, size down on risk' levers (money_pyramid, dd_sizer, edge_monitor, scale_in, vol_scale) are WORSE on than off, on BOTH halves, in the first search that ever varied them together: median fit +0.165 on vs +0.276 off, median HELD-OUT +0.024 on vs +0.160 off, n=106 trials that traded. The joint search was the stated objection to the single-lever experiments that shelved them; it reproduces their verdict. CAVEAT: dd_sizer/edge_monitor/vol_scale show near-identical numbers, so they are largely ON TOGETHER in one seed cluster and this is closer to one verdict than five; scale_in has n=4. READING: the concept is not refuted, the TRIGGER is. All five react to the BOOK'S OWN equity and recent trades - a noisy, backward-looking signal. Nothing here says an EXOGENOUS risk trigger fails, because the book has never had one. That is A87.

title: the companion statistics leaked the held-out years
result: FOUND AND FIXED. The objective was always clean (returns the fit half only), but months_won, worst_month, worst_drawdown and mandate_years were computed over ALL EIGHT years and printed beside the fit score on the console, the live heartbeat and the public page. Surfaced while ranking fit-side statistics by how well they predict the held-out score: mandate_years scored rho +0.65 against a number it partly CONTAINED. No automated selection ever used them; a human ranking trials by the page would have been selecting on 2024-2025 unknowingly. Every companion now carries its half in its name (fit_*, holdout_*, all_*), guarded by three tests.

title: correlation is not selection - judge objectives by the selection experiment
note: Measured 2026-09-04 on 103 trials that traded. Fit-side rank correlation with the held-out score: FIT years>=30% +0.443, mean min(ret,30%) +0.404, FIT score +0.395, worst FIT year +0.339. But the SELECTION experiment (rank on the fit half, read the held-out score of what you would ship) reverses two of them: 'mandate only' has the second-best correlation and picks a book scoring +0.013 held-out, because its top is a degenerate corner. Population correlation says nothing about the quality of the TOP. Any future objective change must be judged by the selection experiment, not by rho. Rescoring completed trials is free - no compute.

title: six workers were doing the work of one and a half
result: FOUND AND FIXED, the largest throughput defect in the study. At 168 completed trials there were only 102 DISTINCT parameter points: 39% of all evaluations duplicated, and after the 96 enqueued seeds were exhausted and TPE took over, 74% of every trial re-ran a point another worker was computing at that moment. Cause: every worker built TPESampler(seed=20260904) and read the same study state through the same SQLite file, so all six drew the identical next point. Fix is two parts - a per-process seed (from the pid, the only identifier guaranteed distinct among LIVE workers) so the six are different draws, and constant_liar=True so they are AWARE of each other: Optuna scores in-flight trials as losses so a point somebody is already evaluating stops looking attractive. Expected effect: roughly 4x the distinct points per hour from the same hardware. Guarded by three tests.

title: a comment broke the watchdog and every daemon with it
result: A comment line placed between `Start-Process -FilePath "python" `` ` and its -ArgumentList made watchdog.ps1 a parse error: PowerShell's backtick continues the line and a comment cannot be continued onto. The watchdog runs with $ErrorActionPreference=SilentlyContinue from a scheduled task, so the only symptom was six optimizer workers that stayed dead. Silently, the autoloop, pulse, cf_pusher and wall_listener would also have stayed dead the moment any of them stopped - a single unparseable file disables the entire 24/7 circuit. Fleet was down ~10 min. Fixed, and test_the_watchdog_script_actually_parses now shells out to PowerShell's own parser so this can never again be discovered by noticing that nothing is running.

title: cross-asset training corpus - more INDEPENDENT episodes, not more rows
note: Operator: train on equities, FX, gold, NASDAQ - any risk asset that moves similarly - so the model recognises more chart shapes. STRONGEST of the data ideas, but the reason usually given for it is the wrong one. We already hold 27 Binance symbols x ~293k 15m bars = ~8M rows. That is not a small dataset by row count. It is a TINY dataset by INDEPENDENT OBSERVATIONS: alt-to-BTC correlation runs 0.7-0.9, so crypto is close to one risk factor sampled 27 times. For a book that holds multi-day trends, the effective sample is the number of distinct trend EPISODES - order 10^3 over eight years, not 10^6. Every extra crypto symbol adds rows and almost no information. Equity indices, FX, rates, metals and energy add episodes genuinely independent of the crypto cycle. Precedent is strong and public: time-series momentum is one of the most replicated cross-asset effects there is (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012; Asness-Moskowitz-Pedersen 2013), and the systematic-macro industry pools exactly this way. IMPLEMENTATION: pooled training with an asset embedding + vol-normalised features (returns over trailing realised vol) so a 60%-vol alt and a 12%-vol index sit on one scale. HAZARDS to handle explicitly: (a) crypto is 24/7, equities and FX are not - sessions, weekend gaps and overnight jumps break a 15m bar grid; consider learning the shared representation at daily or 4h and keeping 15m only for crypto execution; (b) survivorship and point-in-time index membership; (c) licensing and cost beyond free daily bars; (d) the evaluation stays crypto - this is a cross-asset model that trades BTCUSDT, not a new universe to trade.

title: reference-market state as INPUT features (DXY, gold, NASDAQ, VIX, 2y/10y, oil)
note: Distinct from A87 (scheduled macro EVENTS) and from A95 (training ON other assets). This is the cheapest of the three: daily closes of a dozen reference series as continuous CONTEXT inputs to the existing brain. The operator's intuition that gold, FX and equities relate to crypto is measurable and time-varying - BTC's correlation to NASDAQ was near zero before 2020 and materially positive through 2020-2022. That instability is the point: it is a regime feature, not a constant. Free from public daily sources. Same point-in-time discipline as A87 - a level revised later is a leak. SEQUENCE: do this BEFORE A95. It is days of work rather than weeks and it tests the same hypothesis - that other markets carry information for this book - at a fraction of the cost.
result: EXAM 1 WON, 2026-09-07, and by the widest margin any candidate has managed. train_until=2024, exam 2025, champion band+risk verbatim, IDENTICAL pooled data (2,514,806 bars / 2,007,953 train windows in both arms and the control - the reference panel covers 2018 onward with no gaps, so not one training row was lost to warm-up). Only the feature count differs, 44 -> 52. control -6.54% DD 21.9% 72 trades; reference alone +0.98% DD 11.8% 116 trades; reference + recency 2y +20.44% DD 11.5% 75 trades. THE DRAWDOWN IS THE HEADLINE: both arms roughly halved it, and drawdown is a steadier property than return. A96b running with a prediction registered in advance - recency alone lost the 2024 exam by 30 points, so the combination arm's fate on 2024 separates 'the reference columns work' from 'the recency lever found 2025'.

title: pretrained time-series foundation models as voters or feature extractors
note: Operator: big firms have released trained models - could we drop one into the decision tree, or even make it the main engine, or run several at once. Worth testing, with a specific framing. Candidates as of my knowledge (VERIFY current releases and licences before use): Amazon CHRONOS (T5-based, Apache-2.0), Google TIMESFM, Salesforce MOIRAI, IBM GRANITE-TTM / TinyTimeMixers (small enough to be free on a 4060), Nixtla TIMEGPT (API, not local). HONEST EXPECTATION: these are trained to minimise forecast error on the LEVEL of general time series - electricity, traffic, retail, M4 - and financial returns are close to unforecastable in level. A zero-shot directional edge on 15m crypto is unlikely. The realistic use is as a frozen ENCODER: its internal representation of the recent window becomes extra features for our own head, or it runs as one more voter in the consensus beside the oracle net. 'Main engine' is the least likely outcome and must be judged, never assumed. CHEAP FIRST TEST: TTM or Chronos-small, frozen, embeddings into the existing meta-labeller, paired A/B against the champion. Days, not weeks. And see A98 before any of it touches a number.

title: CONTAMINATION AUDIT - a pretrained model can be a lookahead vector
note: THE GUARD THAT MUST EXIST BEFORE A97 OR A88. Any externally pretrained model carries its training corpus inside it. If that corpus covers 2018-2026 financial series, or news, or web text, then running it over 2025 is NOT out of sample - the weights already saw what happened. The model does not need to be handed the future to leak it; it memorised it. This is far more dangerous than a mis-shifted feature, because nothing in our pipeline can detect it: every timestamp is correct and the leak lives inside the weights. It applies to forecasting foundation models (their corpora often include crypto and equity series), to any sentiment model, and to every LLM contemplated in A88. RULE TO ADOPT: for each external model establish (1) its training-data CUTOFF and (2) whether the corpus plausibly contains our assets. A model may only be evaluated on data AFTER its cutoff. A model whose cutoff postdates 2026 cannot be used in this project at all, because our exam year sits inside its memory. Where the cutoff is unknown or undocumented, treat it as contaminated. Corollary worth stating plainly: a model with a 2024 cutoff is legitimate on 2025 and 2026 - a real option, just a far narrower evaluation window than we are used to.

title: the v2/v3 ladder - yes, but AFTER the measuring instrument is fixed
note: Operator: build a v2, a v3, each with more data and more complexity, each more intelligent. Agreed as a direction and NOT as the next step. Evidence from this repository, this week: two candidates doubled the research score and both LOST the sealed year; the fit leader of the current 33-lever search is ahead on the fitted years and BEHIND the incumbent out of sample. Our binding constraint is not capacity, it is the ability to tell a real improvement from a lucky one. Adding parameters to a system that cannot yet measure itself does not make it more intelligent - it makes it wrong faster and more convincingly. ORDER: A100/A101 (honest measurement) -> A96 (cheap new information) -> A95 (more independent episodes) -> then capacity. Note A95 is itself the best regulariser available: more independent data raises the complexity a model can carry without overfitting, so it belongs BEFORE the bigger net, not after it.

title: purged and embargoed cross-validation, then combinatorial purged CV
note: Our selection instrument is a single fit/holdout split: six years fit, two held out. Two problems. (1) LEAKAGE AT THE SEAM - labels are built from forward windows, so a bar late in 2023 carries a label that resolves inside 2024, which means the fit half contains information about the held-out half. Standard fix: PURGE observations whose label windows cross the boundary and add an EMBARGO after it (Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning, ch.7). (2) ONE SPLIT IS ONE SAMPLE - a single held-out number carries enormous variance, which is exactly why our held-out readings wobble by more than the differences we are trying to detect. Combinatorial purged CV builds MANY held-out paths from the same history and turns 'is this better' from a coin flip into a distribution. Attacks the actual bottleneck, costs no new data.

title: multiple-testing correction - we have earned the right to be suspicious of ourselves
note: We have now evaluated hundreds of configurations against the same history. The maximum of N noisy estimates is biased upward by roughly sigma*sqrt(2*ln N) even when every configuration is worthless - at N=500 that is about 3.5 standard deviations of pure selection luck. That is a sufficient explanation for the pattern we keep hitting: a leader that looks strong on the record and reverts out of sample. ADOPT: log the effective number of trials behind every reported leader and discount for it (deflated Sharpe ratio, Bailey & Lopez de Prado 2014, or the simple expected-maximum correction). A candidate should clear the bar for the number of attempts that produced it, not the bar for one attempt. This is a REPORTING change, free, and it would have flagged both of this week's failed candidates before we spent a sealed reading on them.

title: ensemble across seeds and architectures before ensembling across model families
note: Before importing a foundation model to run beside ours (A97), take the cheaper version of the same idea: train the SAME architecture under several seeds and average the signals. Variance reduction is the most reliable free gain in noisy-label learning, it needs no new data, and the 192 and 256 channel nets already on disk are two thirds of an ensemble. It also gives A97 an honest baseline: if averaging five seeds of our own net captures most of the gain, a foundation model has to beat THAT, not beat a single seed.

title: the champion is fed 96 bars and can only SEE 15 of them
rationale: Measured 2026-09-05 by gradient probe on the shipping net, not deduced from config: push a window through OracleNet and ask which input timesteps the output depends on. EXACTLY 15 of the 96 bars have a non-zero gradient. The other 81 are read from disk, standardised, copied to the GPU and multiplied by nothing. window=96 (24h), channels=[192,192,192] -> dilations 1,2,4 -> receptive field 1+2*(1+2+4)=15 bars = 3h45m. Meanwhile the TEACHER is a 3% zigzag whose hold-runs last DAYS. So the student is asked to predict a multi-day swing state from under four hours of context, and the twenty hours of features we prepare for every decision are decoration. This is not a tuning question, it is a mismatch between the label's horizon and the model's memory. It also reframes two earlier results: P32 'confirmed the context window' at 96 bars, but changing the window could never have mattered - the net could not see past bar 15 either way. NO CODE NEEDED: ModelConfig.resolved_dilations derives dilations from the LENGTH of channels (2**i for i in range(len(channels))), so six blocks give 1,2,4,8,16,32 and a receptive field of 127 bars, covering the window with room to spare, at ~2x the parameters of a model that is only 256k.
expect: a net that can see the whole window it is given should track the oracle's multi-day swings materially better; if it does not, the label horizon rather than the architecture is what limits us, which is itself worth knowing
kill: if the 6-block net does not beat the 3-block champion on the held-out method, the receptive field was not the binding constraint and this closes as a measured negative
result: TWO-LEVEL ANSWER, 2026-09-05. NET level: transformation - val net return -31.3% -> +315.6% per symbol after costs on lower accuracy (66.2 -> 63.3), the A108 number moving exactly as predicted. BOOK level, champion band+risk verbatim: FIT +0.3196 vs +0.2805, HELD-OUT +0.2019 vs +0.1643 - the first candidate ever to win the held-out half - and then SEALED 2026: -18.04% vs +25.71%, 250 trades, DD 24.3%. The reading was bought by the pre-registered gate and is recorded in sealed_readouts.jsonl. AUTOPSY: the fit/holdout split is honest for thresholds but NOT for nets - the net trained through ~mid-2024, so 'held-out' 2024 was inside its training data and the FIT years (+302%..+9148% at 3-10% DD) were memorisation; the only genuinely unseen year, 2025, showed the true (small) signal: +3.72% vs -1.49%. The receptive-field hypothesis stays OPEN, now tested by the honest instrument: A109 walk-forward.

title: the vector memory of past decisions was BUILT and TESTED and never connected
rationale: Operator asked (2026-09-05) about vector databases of candles to associate patterns. We already wrote it: quantlab_system06/vectormem.py, 137 lines, with tests/test_vectormem.py, carrying the hard part - the leakage rule that a neighbour is admissible only if its outcome RESOLVED strictly before the query bar, with the index built in expanding blocks. A74 is marked 'built'. But grep finds ZERO references to it anywhere else in the package: it is not in modules/, no module wraps it, the orchestrator has never seen it. It is a finished component that has never once influenced a decision or been measured. Worth finishing precisely because it is a THIRD inductive bias: the TCN learns convolutions, the tree learns axis-aligned splits, and this one remembers - non-parametric and local, strongest exactly where the other two are weakest, on rare configurations. And it is the only one that can say 'I have never seen anything like this': a far k-th neighbour is an honest abstention signal rather than a confident guess.
expect: a modules/vectormem.py wrapper voting like the others, off by default, then a paired A/B
kill: if hit-rate at small k carries no information beyond the tree, close it honestly and delete the module rather than leaving another unwired component on disk
result: RETIRED by pre-registered kill criterion, 2026-09-05. Probe on 741,154 decision bars (14 champion symbols, tree's A32 features, tree's 8h forward label, 12 expanding blocks so neighbours are only ever already-resolved): memory k=25 edge +0.022 (51.3% top quartile vs 49.1% bottom, base 50.1%); a logistic regression under the IDENTICAL protocol - same admissible index rows, same standardisation, same outcome - edge +0.061 (53.6% vs 47.5%). The memory knows something, and a parametric fit on the same information knows it three times better: it is a worse tree, not a third inductive bias. Module + tests deleted per the kill criterion (recoverable from git history, commit d71bd96 and earlier); evidence in rnd/a74_vectormem_probe_2026-09-04.json. What would REOPEN it: a different memory - outcomes of the BOOK'S trades rather than raw bars, or distance used only as an abstention signal - is a new idea and files as one.

title: learn a codebook of window SHAPES and feed the code as a categorical feature
rationale: Operator, 2026-09-05: 'maybe train with patterns'. The original version of that idea, and genuinely different from what we do now. Today every feature is a per-bar scalar and the net must rediscover 'this shape' from scratch inside its convolutions. Instead: take the 96-bar windows, vol-normalise them, cluster them (k-means, or a VQ-VAE codebook of a few hundred entries) FITTED ON TRAINING ROWS ONLY, and hand the net the code id plus the distance to its centroid. That gives the model an explicit vocabulary of market shapes and, like the vector memory, a usable 'this window resembles nothing I was trained on' signal. Cheap, unfashionable, and it composes with everything - it is extra columns, not a new model. HAZARD: the codebook is fitted, so it is a standardiser and obeys the same rule - fit on the training slice, export with the model, never refit on evaluation data.
expect: a small number of codes should dominate the oracle's hold state if chart shape carries the information the operator believes it does; if the codes are uninformative that is a real answer about pattern recognition on this data
kill: no lift over the champion features in a paired A/B

title: the trainer bags N seed-varied nets and the champion was trained with N=1
rationale: Operator, 2026-09-05: 'maybe let's train and use many'. The capability is already there - train(ensemble=N) trains N seed-varied nets and averages their probabilities, saving oracle_net.pt, oracle_net_1.pt and so on. The shipping champion's model card says ensemble: 1. So the single most reliable free gain in noisy-label learning is implemented, tested and switched off. Averaging seeds reduces variance without touching bias, needs no new data, and is the honest baseline any foundation model (A97) must beat: if five seeds of our own net capture most of the gain, an imported model has to beat THAT, not beat one seed. Sequence after A103 so the ensemble bags the better architecture rather than the current one.
expect: a smaller gap between validation and held-out performance, and less seed-to-seed lottery in the numbers we compare configurations by - which is also a direct attack on A101
kill: if 5 seeds do not beat 1 on the held-out method, seed variance is not what is hurting us
result: WON the first walk-forward exam, 2026-09-05: train_until=2024, exam 2025 - single 192x3 seed -6.54% DD 21.9% 72 trades; ensemble of 5 +6.46% DD 16.4% 45 trades. Thirteen points with lower drawdown and fewer trades: the variance-reduction signature (marginal entries cancel across seeds), not the luck signature. FIRST candidate change ever to win a walk-forward A/B. Second independent exam (A112: train<=2023, exam 2024) running before any sealed spend - three research-side winners in a row lost the sealed year, so one exam year does not buy a reading any more. | RETIRED by A113: 1 win in 3 walk-forward exams, and the series adjudication goes to the single seed on the mandate lens.

title: every feature is 15m; the book holds for days
rationale: All 44 columns are computed on the 15m panel. Even with A103's fix the model's longest view is 127 bars, ~32 hours. A swing the 3% oracle labels can run a week or more. Adding the SAME stationary features computed on 4h and daily bars (aligned causally, forward-filled to the 15m grid, so a daily value only appears after that day closes) gives long-horizon context at a fraction of the cost of extending the window. This is the standard multi-timeframe construction and it composes with A103 rather than competing with it. HAZARD, and it is the whole implementation: forward-filling a daily bar is the easiest lookahead in this repository. The daily value for day D must not be visible to any 15m bar inside day D.
expect: the trend/regime columns should carry most of the lift; the oscillators probably add noise
kill: no lift in a paired A/B once the fill is causally correct
