title: the champion net's own validation says it LOSES money after costs
rationale: Read off research/system06/_w192/model_card.json, 2026-09-05: val_gross_return +1.58, val_net_return -0.31, val_buy_hold +1.02, symbols_beating_bh 2 of 14, val_accuracy 66.2%. So on its own validation slice the raw net turns a +158% gross into a -31% net, and beats buy-and-hold on two symbols out of fourteen. Everything the strategy earns is therefore produced by the layers AROUND the net - the hysteresis band, the risk layer, concentration, stops - not by the net's directional skill. That is worth stating plainly because it reorders the whole improvement queue: 66% accuracy on a hold/flat label sounds like a working predictor and is not one at trading frequency. It is also the strongest argument for A103 (the net may simply be blind) and the strongest caution against A99 (a bigger net on top of the same blindness).
expect: after A103, val_net_return is the first number to read - if a net that can see the window still loses money gross-to-net, the label or the horizon is wrong, not the capacity
kill: n/a - this is a diagnosis, not a proposal

title: walk-forward is the ONLY honest instrument for net-level changes
rationale: Three candidates beat the champion on research measures and lost sealed 2026: P47, A83, and A103 - which had won the held-out half first. The split cannot police a net that trained inside it. The 2026-08-29 mandate already named walk-forward (train <= X, judge on X+1) and train(train_until=) implements it. First A/B running: 192x3 vs 192x6, train_until=2024, exam = 2025 alone, champion band+risk verbatim. RULE ADOPTED: sealed readings for net-family candidates now require a walk-forward win, not a research-split win.
expect: if the receptive field matters out of sample, wf192x6 beats wf192x3 on 2025
kill: wf192x6 <= wf192x3 on 2025 retires the deep-field claim at book level
result: ANSWERED 2026-09-05, decisively. Exam 2025 (never seen by either net, champion band+risk verbatim): wf192x3 -6.54% DD 21.9% 72 trades; wf192x6 -25.84% DD 29.8% 176 trades. The deep-field claim RETIRES at book level per the pre-registered kill. TWO lessons: (1) the 15-bar reach is a structural REGULARISER - the blind net generalises better because it cannot memorise the long context; with ~10^3 independent trend episodes, reach+capacity buys memorisation, which is A95's argument confirmed by experiment (more independent data must come before more model). (2) THE INSTRUMENT WORKS: walk-forward agreed with sealed 2026 in direction AND signature (trade inflation + bleed), the first selection instrument in this project that has pointed the same way as the exam. Walk-forward is now the standing gate for any net-level change.

title: weight training toward RECENT years - the market of 2020 is not the market of 2025
rationale: Operator: the market evolves (capital volumes, competing algorithms); what worked in 2020 did not work in 2025, so the model should lean on data closest to today. Standard and sound: exponential sample decay by age (half-life a tunable lever, e.g. 2-4 years) inside train(), composing with the existing uniqueness weighting. It is ALSO the honest version of his 'include 2025 in training' instinct: adoption-time retraining already uses everything through 2025; recency weighting makes the model CARE more about the recent regime without discarding the old episodes that regularise it. Test walk-forward (train<=2024 exam 2025), one lever alone, per the one-at-a-time rule.
expect: better 2025 exam at equal architecture; if the effect is big, it also explains part of why research-era selection keeps failing the forward year
kill: no walk-forward improvement at any reasonable half-life
result: EXAM 1 WON, 2026-09-06 (train<=2024, exam 2025, champion band+risk verbatim, one lever): control no-decay -6.54% DD 21.9% 72 trades; half-life 4y -6.30% DD 17.7% 71 trades; half-life 2y +1.16% DD 15.6% 86 trades. Two properties the ensemble's exam-1 win did NOT have: (a) the response is ORDERED with the lever - weak decay reproduces the control almost exactly, strong decay improves it, which a coin flip does not do; (b) the gain arrives with LOWER drawdown, so it is not return bought with risk. Still only one exam year. A110b running: half-life 2y on train<=2023 / exam 2024 against the measured +22.36% control, plus an exploratory 1y arm that adopts nothing and starts its own series if it wins. | REFUSED by A110b: 1 win in 2 exams.

title: the joint threshold search is CLOSED, and its answer is a real finding
result: 1,668 trials, 1,602 distinct points, 33 levers, TPE with per-pid seeds and constant_liar. Only 10/1607 traded trials beat the champion on the FITTED years (1%), and only 23/1607 on the held-out half (1%). The best-on-fit gains +0.0160 on the years it could see and LOSES -0.0154 on the years it could not. Rank correlation fit-vs-held-out +0.681, so the search is not noise - it transfers in general and stops transferring at the top, which is the signature of an optimum already reached rather than of a broken instrument. CONCLUSION: the champion's thresholds are at a generalising optimum; further threshold search is not where the next gain lives. The operator's question - 'what have all the Bayesian tests served for' - is answered: they proved a negative that we would otherwise have kept paying to re-test one lever at a time, and they did it for the whole tree jointly, which no single-lever experiment could.

title: walk each threshold finely, ONE at a time, and print the actual curve
rationale: Operator, 2026-09-07: 'going from 0.75 to 0.72 or 0.78 HAS to produce a change - it cannot be that the initial values happen to be the best in the world.' The objection is fair and two claims had been conflated in my report. (1) 'moving a threshold changes nothing' is FALSE and the study never said it - all 1,607 trading trials produced different books. (2) 'no move IMPROVES the years it was not fitted to' is what was measured, and it is far narrower. What a JOINT search cannot show is the SHAPE around the incumbent, because 33 levers moved at once. This walks each lever across a fine grid with everything else pinned at the champion - the derivative he has been asking to see.
expect: visible curves; a peak away from the incumbent on any lever is a candidate
kill: n/a - a measurement, both answers informative

title: screen with the vectorised proxy, confirm with the real engine - measured 19x
rationale: Operator, 2026-09-07: 'a 10-year backtest changing values can take a lot of time. Imagine 5,000 combinations. How do we configure this to go fast?' MEASURED TODAY, not estimated: the real engine costs 185 s per evaluation. quantlab_system06/fast_portfolio - a vectorised numpy simulator written for exactly this and IMPORTED BY autoloop BUT NEVER CALLED (the same built-and-unwired shape vectormem had) - costs 9.51 s. 19x. 5,000 combinations go from 43 h on six workers to 2.2 h. THE CATCH, stated first: the proxy implements 7 of the 33 levers (enter, exit_, min_hold, max_positions, position_fraction, stop_loss, trail_stop) and fills at the bar's close instead of the next open. It is a SCREEN, not a verdict. PREREQUISITE BEFORE ANY USE: measure the rank correlation between proxy score and real score over a sample of points. If the proxy does not RANK like the engine, screening on it is worse than useless - it would concentrate the search on the wrong region and every confirmation afterwards would inherit that bias. High rho earns the two-stage design; low rho retires it. FURTHER HEADROOM: the proxy still runs a Python loop over 292,736 timeline steps. Vectorising or JIT-compiling that is plausibly another 10-100x.
expect: rho > 0.8 between proxy and engine on the 7 shared levers
kill: low rank correlation -> the proxy cannot screen and the two-stage design dies
